disposition_reason: Only Table 4 micronutrients (P, Fe, Zn, Se) in six dipping sauce powder formulations are food measurements, and they lack units; cadmium is a rat dosing agent, not a measured contaminant.

study.design: product development and rat feeding study of propolis-fortified dipping sauce powders
study.method: AAS (PerkinElmer 3300) for Fe, P, Se, Zn per AOAC (Latimer)

findings.material_label: Dipping sauce powder (chickpea, shrimp shell and dried tomato base)
findings.integrity_flag: Table 4 prints no unit for P, Fe, Zn and Se, and the Methods do not state one; value not converted.
findings.notes: Mean ± SE; letters are significance groupings. AAS determination. Dry-weight basis stated for proximate analysis.

unresolved: No heavy metal was measured in any sauce; cadmium appears only as cadmium chloride dosed to rats (5 mg/kg body weight) to induce testicular toxicity.
Table 4 micronutrient values have no printed unit; values kept verbatim with value_ugkg null.
Rat tissue and serum results are biological data and not recorded.
